title: Transitive vs. Intransitive Psychological Shifts (-ít/-tat vs. -ul/-ül/-ódik)

sections.title: The Two Faces of Emotional Change
sections.content: In English, a single labile verb often serves both transitively and intransitively ('The music calmed him' / 'He calmed down'; 'The conflict deepened' / 'This deepened the conflict'). Hungarian strictly separates these two valencies through verb morphology. Transitive verbs in -ít or -tat require an external stimulus or agent as subject and an accusative experiencer (-t): A hír megnyugtatta a kapitányt ('The news calmed the captain'); A vita elmélyítette a válságot ('The debate deepened the crisis').

sections.title: Middle and Unaccusative Suffixes (-ul/-ül, -ódik/-ődik, -szik)
sections.content: When the psychological or mental shift unfolds internally within the subject without an accusative object, Hungarian uses -ul/-ül, -ódik/-ődik (often with -ik conjugation), or -szik/-ik stems: A kapitány lassan megnyugodott ('The captain slowly calmed down'); A feszültség feloldódott ('The tension dissolved'); A két barát elidegenedett egymástól ('The two friends grew alienated from each other'); A kutató elmélyült a munkában ('The researcher became absorbed in the work').

sections.title: Key B2 Psychological & Cognitive Valency Pairs

items.spanish: A különös álom egész napra felzaklatta a kapitányt.
items.english: The strange dream agitated the captain for the entire day.

items.spanish: Az őszinte beszélgetés után a görcsös szorongás végre feloldódott benne.
items.english: After the honest conversation, the tense anxiety finally dissolved within him.

items.spanish: A hosszan tartó hallgatás fokozatosan elidegenítette egymástól a házastársakat.
items.english: The prolonged silence gradually alienated the spouses from each other.

items.spanish: Amikor elmélyült az önvizsgálatban, megértette a félelmei valódi okát.
items.english: When he became absorbed in self-examination, he understood the real cause of his fears.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Never use a transitive -ít/-tat verb without an object to mean an inner change: say 'A kapitány megnyugodott' (NOT '*A kapitány megnyugtatott').
